messages:
sanjay: apac peering alert — starting thread. BGP session to transit-provider-3 in ap-south1 flapped ~10:03 UTC, multiple edge routers marked DOWN, we’re seeing 30-40% packet loss and control-plane churn. GPU pool registration from ap-south1 workers failing intermittently. P95 provision latency spiked to ~12s. I'm starting traffic redistribution to nearby regions and opening a support bridge.

mireille: on it — opening bridge with support-bridge and paging neteng + ops. Can you paste quick impact summary for CS to send to active customers? :alarm_clock: 

sanjay: impact summary draft — "We're seeing intermittent connectivity between our APAC edge and a transit provider which is causing provisioning delays and elevated request latencies for some customers in ap-south1. We're redistributing traffic away from impacted nodes; no data loss expected. Working on BGP recovery with provider. ETA preliminary 60-90m." Thoughts?

asha: please add that dedicated customers on reserved pools may see transient throttles, and that we're prioritizing SLA tenants in the redistribution. Also include link to bridge.

leo: neteng update pls — do we have health of peering session & route churn logs?

neteng: looking now. BGP neighbor 203.0.113.7 established at 10:01 then flapped 10:03 -> 10:07 -> down at 10:09. Route churn shows withdraws for /24 prefixes covering edge-nodes-ap-south1-*. Suspect upstream BFD timers on their router misbehaving after software push. Escalating to provider NOC.

devops: rolling a fast fix on our side — draining ap-south1 edge nodes from the load balancer to force new allocations in ap-southeast1/eu-west1. Command run: ```for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l region=ap-south1 -o name); do kubectl cordon $n && kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; done```  — starting now.

ops-bot: automated notice: Redispatch job started for region=ap-south1, target regions=[ap-southeast1,ap-east1,eu-west1], batch=50 nodes. ETA for redispatch completion ~ 20m.

mireille: draft status page update (short): "Degraded provisioning and elevated request latency for APAC (ap-south1) due to a transit provider peering issue. Traffic is being redistributed; some customers may experience higher latencies or provisioning delays. Engineering and provider NOC are investigating. Next update in 15 min or when we have ETA." Approve?

asha: approve with SLA note. Add: "Customers on Reserved/Dedicated plans will be prioritized for capacity migration."

leo: oncall infra note — monitoring KV cache eviction rates and GPU registration events. If registration fails for >30% of nodes after redistribution we fallback to on-prem bridge for high-SLA customers.

neteng: provider NOC responded: they've seen an internal BFD storms metric after a control-plane patch. They've rolled back the patch in the affected POP and are re-establishing BGP. They've given an ETA of 45-75 minutes to reach stability.

support-bridge: joining bridge w/ provider NOC now (link: https://zoom.example/bridge-192900). Mirroring logs to the bridge slack thread.

mireille: sending support emails to top 12 active accounts in APAC with the approved language + SLA note. Template pasted to bridge: ```We are experiencing intermittent connectivity between our APAC edge and a transit provider causing provisioning and latency impacts in ap-south1. We are redistributing traffic and prioritizing reserved capacity. Engineering teams and the provider are working on restoration; preliminary ETA 45-75 minutes. We will update on progress every 15 minutes.```

sanjay: progress check 10:25 UTC — redistribution 60% complete, queued tasks for GPU registration resumed; registration success rate at 84% for redistributed nodes. P95 latency dropping from 12s -> 6.8s for redistributed flows. Still seeing 8 nodes not re-registering.

leo: putting a temporary routing rule to prefer cross-region mirror for high-latency tail customers: `route policy: prefer mirror-APAC -> ap-east1 if rtt>120ms AND customer_tier!=free` — applied.

ops-bot: automated alert: GPU pool ap-south1: nodes_unregistered increased -> 8, provisioning_queue_depth decreased -> 40% (after redistribution).

neteng: provider reports BGP sessions flapped again at 10:31 but now stable after rollback, they are monitoring for recurrence.

mireille: posted status page update at 10:35 UTC with the earlier approved copy and link to support-bridge. Customers ACK'ing via support are being batched and prioritized.

asha: internal ask for CS reps: please escalate any customers showing over 2x baseline latencies or failed provisioning to support-bridge with subject tag [APAC-PROV-URGENT].

sanjay: quick log snippet for SRE debug: ```2026-03-18T10:24:12Z WARN provisioner: registration timeout node=edge-asp1-07 err=handshake timeout provider=203.0.113.7```  — looks tied to BGP churn during handshake.

support-bridge: provider NOC just posted: cleared BFD storm, BGP peers re-established, but monitoring convergence. They asked us to keep an eye for residual route flaps for 30m.

leo: recommend keeping traffic redistribution for 30 mins after provider confirms stable, then gradually shift back if register metrics stay >95% for 15 consecutive minutes.

mireille: next public update scheduled 10:50 UTC. If provider gives full clear earlier we'll update sooner.

devops: redistribution complete at 10:40 UTC. All but 2 nodes re-registered. Starting targeted restart of remaining agents (1-2 min per node).

ops-bot: automated notice: redistribution complete, total nodes moved=78, time=17m.

sanjay: 10:47 UTC — remaining 2 nodes fixed after agent restart. Registration success 100%. P95 latencies back to baseline for most APAC routes. Marking incident as "degraded->mitigated".

mireille: posting final status page update: "Root cause: transit provider BFD/control-plane regression causing BGP session flaps. Impact: intermittent provisioning delays and elevated latencies in ap-south1. Mitigation: traffic redistributed and provider rolled back change; nodes re-registered and provisioning normal. ETA met. If you continue to see issues, contact support."

asha: follow-up: ask provider for RCA and mitigation plan for future patches. CS to follow up with impacted customers with post-mortem summary and credits if SLA breached.

leo: logging action items: 1) add BFD anomaly alert to provider health dashboard 2) add automated failover runbook for redispatch 3) verify on-call rotation for neteng NOC coordination.

support-bridge: closing bridge. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
